messages.subject: ping 2
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

in order to check that all is well, I send out here a second "ping"
message: please *everyone* answer with a short line to me *and* John.

John's email somehow didn't make it to the list, so here it is again:

> Claudia and I have had only incomplete response to our request for
> information about how mentors and students are planning to keep in
> touch.
>
> We suspect that you are busy getting going. However, as we plan to
> present a summary of the GSoC activity for R in August, it will help
> us immensely if you keep us informed. Note that our omnibus
> description in no way precludes individual projects from presenting
> at UseR, and we have been told that "late" poster submissions will be
> welcome, though it is now beyond the deadline for talks.
>
> As one mechanism for communication and tracking, Yixuan Qui, Ben
> Bolker and I are using a wiki to record a plan and "diary" of
> activity. We can store files there too, and expand ideas on
> subsidiary pages. We may use a version control system for the code,
> though the wiki can partly carry this function.  The process is a
> bit messy, but has proved successful in two previous projects where
> collaboration between several folk was important, and where we
> wanted to keep a timeline and record of what we did.
>
> If any group wants to do this, I have a macro that sets up a
> Dokuwiki very quickly. Send me email with the name you want for the
> wiki and the usernames, real names and emails, and I'll set one up
> for you on my server. Please let me know who will be the "admin" to
> handle options and users on the wiki. FYI Dokuwiki is used for the R
> wiki, and is pretty vanilla to use. I believe the default I set up
> for such wikis is that only the main page is world-visible. This is
> alterable, of course, but for the open discussion of occasionally
> not-so-bright ideas, I prefer to keep the group closed until there is
> consensus on what to present.

Best,

Claudia

--

messages.subject: AW: ping 2
messages.body_plain:
Daniel,

thanks for your answer. It is not pro forma, though (but that tells me my message should have been clearer): we'll send out such ping messages every once in a while in order to make sure things are going well and that we would realize if they weren't. So please go on responding. As the R projects are basically independent of the R organization, we cannot see from logs of the central version control or the like that work is progressing.

Claudia

messages.subject: Mid term reports soon!
messages.body_plain:
Mentors and students -- please note that the GSoC mid-term reports will be due July 15.
Yes, they come fast. Please start thinking about this and ensure that you have
communicated well what has been done and whether it meets expectations.

We unfortunately appear to already have one "Fail" (that is Google's term) in that one
student has not communicated with his mentor for a while. Thus unfortunately seems to
happen every year. However, we need to respect the aims of the program to produce useful
code. GSoC is not "free money". For those who take the program seriously, there are
generally non-money benefits available, since students become "known" to different
software communities and make contacts that can be helpful in finding study or job positions.

Do let Claudia and I know of any difficulties. Our ability to help may be limited, but we
can try to assist and advise.

Best, JN

Since I am a debutant at GSoC mentoring, I have a some basic questions regarding mid-term reports.

2. How long can the report be?

3. Should the code and results be included?

4. Any other important/useful things include in the report?

Thanks,
Ravi.
